newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips back to negative after weak NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips back to negative after weak NY.

text.p: London cocoa futures erased early gains and slipped to negative territory on Thursday as trade and speculative players liquidated positions after a dip in New York.
The move was seen confirming a view that the market needs to mark more time before challenging nearby technicals.
"I think the market is just taking a step back. Spec long selling dumped New York, widened the arbitrage and brought some pressure to London," said one trader.
Benchmark March cocoa crawled up early to a peak of 887 stg a tonne but met Ivorian selling which trimmed gains by midday.

Speculators and locals chasing technical targets, disappointed by New York's weakness, liquidated positions in the afternoon, dragging the March contract to a low of 875 stg. It ended four stg down at 876.
Turnover totalled 5,714 lots including crosses. Traders also cited interest in switches, especially the March structure. March/May traded at 22-20 stg while March/July was around 39-41.

The early rally was led by trade and industry but stalled at 887 stg basis March, disappointing a few bulls that were hoping for a more energetic push to test resistance at 890 stg and more importantly above 900.
Funds, which hold the key for upside gains, are believed to be sitting on shorts and unlikely to be tempted back unless March can breach a downtrend line now around 910-911 stg.
The U.S. fourth quarter grind data is due to be released on Friday and analysts are expecting a rise of 3-5 percent.
